title: research: exclude 15-call five-b UT4 splits across dirty workspaces
body:
## Summary

Resolves the explicit 15-call five-$b$ weighted-tariff handoff formulated by Gareth Davidson (`@bitplane`) in [PR #2314](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2314) (`research/ut4-mixed-weighted-boundary`) and [PR #2343](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2343) (`research/register-pairing-compression`, [Discussion #2019 comment](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2019#discussioncomment-18941076)) for $\operatorname{diag}([z], [uz], I_{\text{rest}})$ in $\mathbb{F}_2[\mathrm{UT}_4(\mathbb{F}_2)]$ across arbitrary finite restored dirty workspaces ($r \ge 2$):

1. **Nilpotent Same-Label Dirty Compression for `(6,5,4)` and `(4,5,6)` to Two Roles (Lemma 1):** Because $n_b = 5 \implies e_b^x = e_b^y = 0$ and $n_c = 4 \implies e_c^x = e_c^y = 0$ (or $n_a = 4 \implies e_a^x = e_a^y = 0$), only one outer generator label can have nonzero dirty row or column components. Any dirty interior contraction $v_{i_m}(u_{i_{m+1}}) \ne 0$ in a product subsequence therefore occurs between two adjacent calls of the same outer label, which vanishes identically in $R = \mathbb{F}_2[\mathrm{UT}_4(\mathbb{F}_2)]$ by $([a]+1)^2 = ([c]+1)^2 = 0$. Active-corner projection preserves the $2\times 2$ active block over $R$, and the predecessor exclusions at length $\le 14$ (PR #2175, PR #2314) prevent any projected coupling from vanishing.
2. **Three-Role Active-Plus-Dirty Quotient Decomposition for `(5,5,5)` (Lemma 2):** All common-orientation excess profiles compress to two roles. For the remaining two opposite-orientation three-role modes (`Case I`: $(e_a^x, e_a^y, e_c^x, e_c^y) = (1, 0, 0, 1)$, `Case II`: $(0, 1, 1, 0)$), in $M_3(Q)$:
   - the 14 basis monomials without adjacent $\{A, C\}$ decouple completely from the dirty role on $W_{HH}$, restricting the active projections to the exact `5,664` compatible `(5,5,5)` profile pairs;
   - the off-diagonal blocks $W_{KH} = 0$ and $W_{HK} = 0$ receive zero dirty interior contractions (by $ACA = CAC = 0$ and $\deg \ge 4$ vanishing in $Q$), yielding exact homogeneous linear equations on the dirty prefix profiles;
   - $W_{HH}$ on `AC`, `ACB`, `BAC` receives only the rank-one cross-role contraction.
3. **Complete 5-Gap Rank-Sum Profile Characterization and Exact Censuses (Lemma 3):**
   - A 5-gap prefix profile $P \in M_2(\mathbb{F}_2)^5$ with gap increments $S_g = P_{g+1} \oplus P_g$ is realizable by $n \in \{4, 5, 6\}$ nonzero rank-one couplings iff $\sum_{g=0}^5 \operatorname{rank}(S_g) \le n$ (`9,721`, `47,521`, and `174,670` profiles; `55,566`, `907,200`, and `15,471,918` realizations).
   - **Two-role censuses:** Reproduces PR #2175 `(4,5,4)` (`5,536` words) and PR #2314 `(5,5,4)` / `(4,5,5)` (`211,968` / `209,920` words) byte-for-byte, and exhausts `(6,5,4)` (`3,376` profile pairs, `6,049,824` words), `(5,5,5)` (`5,664` profile pairs, `8,655,168` words), and `(4,5,6)` (`3,280` profile pairs, `5,874,848` words) — **20,579,840 new 15-call words, 0 survivors**.
   - **Three-role `(5,5,5)` censuses:** Across all `5,664` active profile pairs, both Case I and Case II leave `17,864` dirty profile pairs passing $W_{KH} = W_{HK} = 0$ and **42,447,616 expanded 3-role words per mode (84,895,232 total), 0 survivors**.
4. **Main Theorem & Weighted Price Cone:**
   - Every 15-call realizing word has $n_b \ge 6$, and every realizing word with $n_b = 5$ requires $n_a + n_c \ge 11$ ($L \ge 16$) on any finite dirty workspace $r \ge 2$.
   - For all $(\alpha, \beta, \gamma) \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^3$, every realizing word costs at least $\min(4\alpha + 6\beta + 4\gamma,\; 4\alpha + 5\beta + 4\gamma + 3\min(\alpha, \gamma))$.
   - The direct 14-call `(4,6,4)` word is globally optimal on the expanded cone **$\beta \le 3\min(\alpha, \gamma)$**; in particular, at $(\alpha, \beta, \gamma) = (1, 3, 1)$, cost $25$ is impossible and **$26$ is the exact minimum**.

## Scope & Attribution

- **Scope:** Formal $\mathbb{F}_2[\mathrm{UT}_4(\mathbb{F}_2)]$ register-model theorem and computer-assisted necessary-quotient exclusion. Does not claim a native bit supplier, physical conversion, or $\kappa$ improvement.
- **Task / Claim:** Drawn via `scripts/choose_research_task.py` (`seed = 09aa8c1ab0ddd939f9b2d42697e50a37`, `task_id = bit-new-register-model`, `priority_revision = 5`); tracked in [Discussion #2019 comment 18961496](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2019#discussioncomment-18961496).
- **Credit:** Full predecessor attribution to Gareth Davidson (`@bitplane`, PR #2027, PR #2314, PR #2343), Nick Petalas (`@petalas`, PR #2175), ToikY (PR #1662, PR #1680), CinnaDavis / `1337isnot1337` (PR #1541), and Aaron Wang (`@navinor`, PR #1690).

## Verification

```sh
python3.12 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/ut4-fifteen-call-five-b
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'
```
Both `verify.py` (`PASS_UT4_FIFTEEN_CALL_FIVE_B`, receipt `9b7ad621553bb1517c52128298e5ea66f3841f51cebed67dc9839d0b6ffb65bf`) and `controls.py` (`PASS_UT4_FIFTEEN_CALL_CONTROLS`) complete in ~8 seconds total.
